title: In 1990 This Was Farmland — Now It's China's Tallest Skyline | China Travel Expert
description:
In 1990, the east bank of Shanghai's Huangpu River — Pudong — was mostly farmland and industrial waterfront. That year it became China's first financial special economic zone, and in about three decades it grew into one of the tallest skylines on Earth.

Stand on the Bund, the 1920s colonial waterfront, and look across the river: Lujiazui now holds the world's first three adjacent "supertall" towers — the Shanghai Tower at 632 m, the Shanghai World Financial Center at 492 m, and the Jin Mao Tower at 420.5 m — plus the Oriental Pearl. It's the fastest skyline transformation of its size anywhere.

🧭 Expert Tip: You don't need a paid observation deck — the free view is from the Bund promenade at dusk, when the old west bank and the lit-up towers of Pudong face off across the water.

1990年这里还是农田，30年后浦东陆家嘴长出了世界第一组三座紧邻的超高层——上海中心632米。
